name: EU Artificial Intelligence Act
description: Harmonised rules on artificial intelligence across the EU internal market, establishing a risk-based classification framework with strict obligations for high-risk AI systems and transparency requirements.
applicability_conditions: Providers placing AI systems on the EU market or putting them into service in the EU
Deployers of AI systems that have their place of establishment or are located within the EU
Providers and deployers of AI systems located in a third country where the output produced by the AI system is used in the EU

requirements.title: Prohibition of Unacceptable-Risk AI Practices
requirements.normalized_requirement: The organization shall screen all AI systems to ensure they do not deploy subliminal distortion, exploit vulnerabilities of specific groups, conduct social scoring, engage in individual predictive policing, compile untargeted facial recognition databases, infer emotions in workplace/education (except medical/safety), or employ real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement except strictly permitted.
requirements.applicability: All AI systems in scope of EU AI Act
requirements.implementation_guidance: Implement mandatory intake screening checkpoint verifying that no AI system performs prohibited practices before architectural approval.

chapters.title: High-Risk AI Systems — Requirements for Providers

requirements.title: Risk Management System
requirements.normalized_requirement: A continuous, iterative risk management system shall be established, implemented, documented and maintained throughout the entire lifecycle of high-risk AI systems, identifying known and foreseeable risks and adopting suitable mitigation measures.
requirements.applicability: High-risk AI systems (Annex III / safety component Annex I)
requirements.implementation_guidance: Document a lifecycle risk management procedure specific to AI, conduct pre-deployment risk evaluations, and track residual risks.

requirements.title: Data and Data Governance
requirements.normalized_requirement: High-risk AI systems which make use of techniques involving the training of models with data shall be developed on the basis of training, validation and testing data sets that meet quality criteria, including bias examination and appropriate data provenance.
requirements.applicability: High-risk AI systems using model training
requirements.implementation_guidance: Maintain data governance protocols, document data provenance, evaluate statistical bias, and audit dataset quality.

requirements.title: Technical Documentation
requirements.normalized_requirement: Technical documentation of a high-risk AI system shall be drawn up before that system is placed on the market or put into service and kept up to date, complying with Annex IV requirements.
requirements.implementation_guidance: Compile comprehensive Annex IV technical documentation including model cards, architecture diagrams, algorithmic choices, and validation results.

requirements.title: Record-Keeping and Automatic Logging
requirements.normalized_requirement: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events ('logs') over the lifetime of the system to ensure traceability of system functioning and post-market monitoring.
requirements.implementation_guidance: Implement automated immutable logging capturing system inputs, outputs, operational periods, and exceptions.

requirements.title: Transparency and Provision of Information to Deployers
requirements.normalized_requirement: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way as to ensure that their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret the system's output and use it appropriately, accompanied by clear instructions for use.
requirements.implementation_guidance: Publish comprehensive deployer instructions for use, detailing capabilities, limitations, intended purpose, and performance metrics.

requirements.title: Human Oversight
requirements.normalized_requirement: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way, including with appropriate human-machine interface tools, that they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which they are in use, with the ability to intervene or stop the system.
requirements.implementation_guidance: Establish human-in-the-loop / human-on-the-loop controls, override mechanisms, and emergency kill-switches.

requirements.title: Accuracy, Robustness and Cybersecurity
requirements.normalized_requirement: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way that they achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity, resilient against errors, faults, data poisoning, and adversarial attacks.
requirements.implementation_guidance: Perform red-teaming, adversarial robustness evaluations, prompt injection testing, and vulnerability management.

chapters.title: Transparency Obligations for Certain AI Systems

requirements.title: Transparency Obligations for Providers and Deployers
requirements.normalized_requirement: Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed so that the natural persons are informed that they are interacting with an AI system; deployers generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content shall disclose that content has been artificially generated or manipulated.
requirements.applicability: AI systems interacting with humans or generating synthetic content
requirements.implementation_guidance: Provide clear AI disclosure banners, machine-readable watermarking, or provenance metadata on synthetic outputs.

requirements.title: Obligations for Providers of General-Purpose AI Models
requirements.normalized_requirement: Providers of general-purpose AI models shall draw up and keep up to date technical documentation, provide documentation to downstream providers, put in place a policy to respect Union copyright law, and publish a sufficiently detailed summary of content used for training.
requirements.implementation_guidance: Maintain GPAI technical dossiers, downstream integration guidance, copyright compliance policy, and public training dataset summaries.
